archetype.name: Game Manager (spot starter)
archetype.definition: A low-risk fill-in who keeps the Ravens on schedule with short, accurate throws and rarely gives the ball away, but offers little downfield and takes too many sacks to lift the offense on his own.

report.headline: A competent, careful fill-in whose sacks cancel much of what his arm earns
report.take:
Huntley is what he has been for six seasons: a capable QB2 who can run Baltimore's offense without wrecking it. In three starts since Lamar Jackson's ankle sprain he has posted 0.107 EPA per dropback, nearly identical to his 0.101 for the season and above the qualifier average of 0.04. That puts him in the middle of the pack (23rd of 45), which is about the best a team can ask of a backup. He protects the ball (0.9% INT rate, 10th), his bad-throw rate of 8.5% is the lowest among charted passers, and he completes 69.8% of his throws. The offense around him helps. Even with three Huntley starts mixed in, Baltimore's passing game ranks 8th in EPA.

The value has a strange shape. His 78 throws under 10 air yards are close to break-even (0.058 EPA). The real gains come from just 28 throws of 10+ yards that add 15.9 EPA, almost all of it from 21 intermediate attempts at 0.703 EPA apiece. That is a hot handful of plays, not a trait. His career has never shown that kind of middle-of-the-field punch, and the deep ball has been 1-of-7. The underlying approach is conservative: intended air yards of 6.69, throws landing 2.25 yards short of the sticks on average, and 23 throws behind the line completed at 91.3%. Those screens inflate the completion rate, which is why Next Gen's CPOE reads -3.24 even though the play-by-play CPOE reads +2.94.

The drag is the sacks, and it is not new. He is pressured on only 16.1% of dropbacks, the 7th-lowest rate, yet he is sacked on 8.6% of them (34th of 45) and turns a third of his pressures into sacks. His pressure-to-sack rate has been high every season of his career. He holds the ball (2.84 seconds), and the extensions don't pay. Nine scrambles have produced zero first downs. His passing EPA totals 11.7, but all his dropbacks together add up to only 5. He is also running less: 19 rushing yards a game, down 18.8 from last season.

Last year's 12.9 CPOE and 0.202 EPA per play over four games were the outlier, and this year's numbers are a regression to his true level, not a decline. Where it goes from here depends almost entirely on Jackson. The coach says Jackson is "in a decent spot" to play Sunday, and the depth chart already lists Huntley as QB2.

strengths.title: Clean, turnover-averse ball placement
strengths.body: He has one interception on 106 attempts and the lowest bad-throw rate among charted passers. A short, rhythm-based approach keeps him out of high-risk windows. His bad-throw rate has improved for two straight seasons, so the accuracy is real, though the near-zero INT rate will drift up some with volume.

strengths.title: Moves the chains on third down
strengths.body: On third down he has been at his best: 0.267 EPA per play and a 46.2% conversion rate against an average of 7.7 yards to go. He completes 74.3% there with a 9.4 CPOE, finding the sticks rather than checking down short of them. It is 39 plays, so treat it as a solid hint rather than a lock.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws carrying the offense
strengths.body: His 21 throws of 10-19 air yards have produced 0.703 EPA each, and they account for most of his passing value. Bateman (0.712 EPA per target) and Cuevas (0.752) have been the beneficiaries. The sample is small and the 57.1% completion rate on those throws comes with a -4.4 CPOE, so expect this to cool.

concerns.title: Sacks wipe out the low pressure rate
concerns.body: He is rarely pressured but goes down often when he is, a career-long pattern rather than a blip. Holding the ball to extend hasn't bought anything: nine scrambles, zero first downs. That gap between his passing EPA and his total dropback EPA is the cost, and it should persist.

concerns.title: No vertical threat
concerns.body: He is 1-of-7 on throws of 20+ air yards and generally throws short of the sticks. Defenses can squat on underneath routes. The middle of the field has also been poor (-15.9 CPOE), consistent with a passer who lives outside the numbers and behind the line.

concerns.title: Andrews targets have been a sinkhole
concerns.body: Fifteen throws to Mark Andrews have cost 10.9 EPA, by far the biggest drag among his targets. A couple of disastrous plays can produce a number like that on so few looks, so it likely evens out. Still, it has been the single biggest leak in his passing so far.

trend.note: His three starts produced 3.4, 4.6 and 3.5 passing EPA, a consistent level even as results went from a win at Atlanta to a 35-13 loss to Cincinnati. The 298 yards in that loss came largely from chasing the game, not a step forward.

nextGame.headline: Soft Bills secondary, but Lamar's ankle decides whether he plays
nextGame.body:
If Huntley starts, this is the best setup he has had. Buffalo's defense ranks last in EPA and 29th against the pass. It allows the 28th-highest explosive-pass rate and 21.8 PPR a game to quarterbacks, 29th in the league. Its sack rate ranks 26th, which matters most for a passer whose main flaw is taking sacks. Buffalo's offense ranks 1st in EPA, and the Ravens are 3.5-point underdogs with a 53.5 total, the highest of any game he has played this year. That points to a script where Baltimore has to keep throwing.

Availability is the whole story. Jackson is listed as out with the ankle sprain, but the coach said he is "in a decent spot" to play, and Huntley already sits at QB2 on the depth chart. If Jackson goes, Huntley is a clipboard holder. On Buffalo's side, starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (89% of snaps) is suspended, thinning a defense already leaking big plays. Ed Oliver is questionable, which would further soften the interior rush. Baltimore guard Olaivavega Ioane (89% of snaps) left the Bengals game with a knee injury and is questionable; his absence would hurt a quarterback who already converts too many pressures into sacks.

keyMatchups.title: Flowers against Buffalo's WR1 coverage
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo has let opposing WR1s score 9.8 PPR a game over their own averages, the worst mark in the league, and allows 0.52 EPA per WR1 target. Zay Flowers has been Huntley's primary read, with 34 targets. That gives him a reliable, efficient outlet without needing the deep ball he doesn't throw.

keyMatchups.title: Weak rush meets his sack problem
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo gets home on just 4.2% of dropbacks, 26th in the league, and may be without Ed Oliver. That is the best possible opponent for a quarterback whose pressure-to-sack rate ranks 28th of 38. If Ioane can't play at guard, that edge shrinks.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script against Buffalo's offense
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's league-best offense makes a trailing, pass-heavy game likely. That inflates attempts and yards, as the Cincinnati loss showed. It also invites the few bad moments he has had: his plays trailing by 9+ have been costly.

nextGame.watch: Jackson's practice status this week; if he is cleared, Huntley doesn't play.

restOfSeason.body:
The likeliest path is that Jackson returns and Huntley goes back to the QB2 role, with essentially no stats. If the ankle lingers or recurs, expect what the three starts showed. He is a steady, mid-pack passer at about 0.1 EPA per dropback, with few turnovers, a high sack rate, and little downfield production. His career says the sacks are permanent. The intermediate efficiency and the near-zero interception rate should both cool, while the Andrews drag should even out. Per start, that means roughly 185-240 passing yards and about one touchdown, with more volume in games where Baltimore trails.

One thing that could add value is the legs. He ran for 37.8 yards a game last season and has been far more conservative this year. A return to designed runs would lift his floor, but nothing in these three starts suggests the coaches want that.
swingFactors: Lamar Jackson's ankle and how many more starts it opens
Whether Ioane's knee keeps him out of the interior line
Game script: trailing raises his volume, not his efficiency

confidence.note: His profile matches six seasons of backup work, but there are only 106 attempts and his role hinges on Jackson's return.
